snip.t: Silicosis: Silica (quartz) dust — Miners, quarry and stone workers, sandblasters, tunnellers, ceramics, masons — Upper-zone nodules, eggshell calcification of hilar nodes, progressive massive fibrosis; high risk of TB (silico-tuberculosis), lung cancer, COPD, autoimmune disease
Coal worker's pneumoconiosis: Coal dust — Coal miners — Small upper-zone nodules, progressive massive fibrosis, Caplan syndrome (rheumatoid arthritis + nodules)
Coal workers' pneumoconiosis: coal dust exposure; small upper-zone opacities and, in severe disease, progressive massive fibrosis.

snip.t: Patients can either present with simple (nodular) silicosis or progressive massive fibrosis (PMF).
Patients with simple silicosis can be asymptomatic, while those with progressive massive fibrosis may have signs and symptoms of chronic respiratory failure.
The nodules may be​come confluent with progressive massive fibrosis.

qs.q: On a chest radiograph, which finding best distinguishes progressive massive fibrosis from simple coal workers’ pneumoconiosis?
o: Large conglomerate opacities in the upper lung fields
Small rounded opacities in the upper zones
qs.e: Progressive massive fibrosis presents as large masses formed by coalescence of nodules. Simple CWP shows only small rounded opacities.

qs.q: What radiographic finding indicates progressive massive fibrosis in chronic silicosis?
o: large opacities >1 cm in upper zones
qs.e: PMF presents as large masses >1 cm in the upper zones; small nodules represent simple silicosis.
